inputs.text: Hey everyone, I just heard about this case out of Wisconsin where a jury convicted Harry Wait on two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft after he requested ballots without consent. He admitted doing it to try proving the voter system is vulnerable to fraud. But from where I stand, this is a clear example of deliberate stunts by those pushing narratives that erode trust in our elections to justify barriers that hit hardest on low-income workers, communities of color, and other historically marginalized groups already fighting systemic discrimination. The real harm isn't any so-called exposure of the system—it's how these actions feed into structural inequality and distract from the need for institutional reforms that protect voting access for the vulnerable rather than preserving the status quo. We should be focusing on safeguards that promote equity and labor rights, not letting bad-faith exploits undermine democracy for everyone.
